summary: OSpec 2.0.2 fixes the generated `docs/project/feature-catalog.md` so its links work: heading anchors keep Unicode (CJK headings no longer anchor to an empty fragment), and hrefs resolve through the project layout (nested-layout projects no longer link through a doubled `.ospec/`). No breaking changes. After upgrading, run `ospec index build` in each project — the catalogue regenerates with working links; no re-migration is needed.
fixed: Heading anchors in `feature-catalog.md` are Unicode-aware. The slugger previously kept ASCII word characters only, so a pure-Chinese section heading anchored to an empty `#` and a mixed heading to fragments like `#-http-`; no rendered link could jump to its section. Anchors now keep Unicode letters and digits, matching how GitHub and VS Code compute heading anchors.

Catalogue hrefs resolve through the project layout. The link base was hardcoded to the classic `docs/project` location while the targets carried the nested-resolved `.ospec/...` prefix, so on a nested-layout project every section and archive link resolved through a doubled `.ospec/` and pointed at nothing. Classic-layout output is byte-identical to before; nested-layout catalogues now render sibling links such as `../features/<doc>.md#<anchor>`. The standalone `build-index` tool twin carries the same fix, and the tool-vs-CLI byte-parity guard now also runs on a nested zh-CN fixture.
